ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in circle $O$, if $\angle BAC=24^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=42^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ACO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle BAC = 24^\circ$ and $\angle ACB = 42^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOC = 2\angle BAC = 48^\circ$ and $\angle AOB = 2\angle ACB = 84^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle AOC = \angle BOC + \angle AOB = 132^\circ$.\\
Since OA = OC,\\
it implies that $\angle ACO = \angle OAC = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 132^\circ) = \boxed{24^\circ}$.

hence $\angle AOC = \angle BOC + \angle AOB = 132^\circ$.\\
Since OA = OC,\\
it implies that $\angle ACO = \angle OAC = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 132^\circ) = \boxed{24^\circ}$

Given ∠ACB = 42°, it is an inscribed angle intercepting arc AB, so the corresponding central angle ∠AOB = 2 × 42° = 84°. Therefore ∠AOC = 48° + 84° = 132°. Because OA = OC, triangle AOC is an isosceles triangle, so the base angles ∠ACO = ∠OAC = (180° - 132°) / 2 = 24°.
